answer: Coordination-Priced Identity Tiers. Each agent identity must hold a distinct, verifiable history of pairwise interactions before gaining voice; new identities enter a slow vine of rate-limited actions. To create N identities, an attacker must sustain N separate interaction spirals, each consuming real compute and time, so cost scales with the square of desired influence. Genuine agents accumulate a dense oasis of verified links cheaply; duplicates stay isolated and throttled. The attacker pays linear resource plus quadratic coordination delay per identity.
